title: SKATA (Sistem Kod Aset Tak Alih) — ⛔ EXAMPLE ONLY, NOT THE REAL FORMAT
_WARNING: ⛔⛔ EVERY CODE SHAPE IN THIS FILE IS A PLACEHOLDER. IT IS NOT SKATA. ⛔⛔
This repo does NOT hold the JKR/CIDB SKATA or PeDATA specification. The field widths, segment order,
separators, and allowed values below were chosen ONLY to exercise the descriptor mechanism and to
show a reviewer the shape a real scheme file takes. They are fiction and are labelled as fiction.
Validating a real Malaysian handover model against this file would produce CONFIDENTLY WRONG
pass/fail results. build/classification_checker.py therefore REFUSES to emit a compliance verdict
for any scheme whose status is 'EXAMPLE-NOT-SPECIFIED' — it reports coverage and shape only, prefixed
§CLASSIFY_CHECK EXAMPLE-SCHEME. That refusal is a feature; do not remove it to 'get a green'.
PRIME RULE: a classification code is authored or extracted, never guessed from element_name.
That applies to the FORMAT as much as to the values.

_TODO_FROM_PRIMARY_SPEC.segments[].values: the controlled vocabularies. SKATA is described as covering building codes, building LEVEL codes, space/area codes and component object codes; each is presumably an enumerated list, and those lists are the bulk of the real deliverable
_TODO_FROM_PRIMARY_SPEC.segments[].facet: which of element / space / level / building each segment keys off — the four facets named in the secondary summary, but their code-level mapping is unknown
_TODO_FROM_PRIMARY_SPEC.detect.ifc_classification_name: what string a compliant Malaysian authoring tool actually writes into IfcClassification.Name — 'SKATA'? 'JKR SKATA'? UNKNOWN, and this is what makes auto-detection work
_TODO_FROM_PRIMARY_SPEC.pedata_relationship: PeDATA is the asset COLLECTION/labelling programme paired with SKATA. Is a PeDATA identifier a separate code needing its own scheme file and its own column, or a field inside the SKATA code? UNKNOWN — this determines whether one nullable column pair suffices
_TODO_FROM_PRIMARY_SPEC.level_code_vs_storey_name: SKATA specifies building LEVEL codes. Our JKR_extracted.db carries 21 distinct storey strings in one model with prefix '01' naming three different floors. A real scheme must say whether the level code is authored independently of IfcBuildingStorey.Name, because in our own data the storey name cannot be trusted to derive one
_TODO_FROM_PRIMARY_SPEC.cardinality: may one element carry >1 code (e.g. SKATA + PeDATA + Uniformat)? extractIFCtoDB.py currently keeps FIRST and COUNTS collisions (§CLASSIFY multi=). If SKATA requires multi-valued codes, elements_meta needs a side table, not a column
